key_insight: Wasserstein approximation by measures supported on orthogonal axes identifies a basis for sparse data representation, with near-parametric frame recovery under mild assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a principled way to select sparse coordinate systems within learned subspaces for unsupervised representation learning.
method: Approximate the data distribution with measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame.
Optimize a nonsmooth objective over the orthogonal group O(d).
Use a coarsely Lipschitz bound to analyze empirical minimizers and locally initialized stochastic gradient optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a recovery rate of Õ_d(n^−1/2) and numerical experiments supporting the theory, but provides no dataset or benchmark details.
watch_item: The stochastic gradient guarantee requires local initialization, and the stated rate can hide dimension-dependent factors.
paper_title: Wasserstein approximation of measures via orthogonal frames: statistical and computational complexities
